title: Concise incident briefing + customer postmortem (draft)
content:
Purpose: This is a compact, customer-facing briefing and short postmortem draft for the service disruption on 2026-11-29. Intended for status.redwood.ai and targeted customer emails. Keep it concise and non-technical; include what happened, impact, mitigation, and next steps.

Incident snapshot:
- Incident ID: INC-4512
- Affected product: Redwood Hosted API - text generation (us-west-2 primary)
- Customer impact: increased response latency and intermittent 5xx errors for generation endpoints
- Start time (first elevated alerts): 2026-11-29 02:17 UTC
- Full mitigation (customer-visible): 2026-11-29 07:03 UTC
- Internal detection -> mitigation timeline summarized below.

Status page update (to publish)
- Status: Partial service disruption — Resolved
- Summary (one sentence): Between 02:17–07:03 UTC on 2026-11-29, a configuration regression in request routing caused elevated latency and intermittent errors for text-generation endpoints in the us-west-2 cluster; the issue has been mitigated and normal service restored.
- Impact: Some customers experienced slow responses (median latency increased from ~90ms to ~1.8s) and occasional 5xx failures for generation calls. No customer data was accessed or lost.
- Current status: Service restored; ongoing validation and additional hardening in progress.
- Next updates: This is the final status update; a short customer postmortem is available below and a detailed internal postmortem is in our Confluence.

Customer-facing postmortem (concise)
What happened:
- A deployment included a routing change intended to shift low-priority traffic to a new spare pool. An unintended mapping edge-case sent a subset of live requests to a pair of worker nodes running an incompatible kernel version, causing request queueing and cascading timeouts under realistic load.

Root cause:
- Regression in routing config + insufficient Canary (sample size too small for this traffic mix) + lack of kernel-version compatibility checks in the deployment gating process.

What we did to mitigate:
- Immediately rolled back the routing change (02:45 UTC).
- Scaled up compatible worker capacity and drained the affected nodes (03:10–05:00 UTC).
- Reverted to previous stable routing policy and disabled the faulty routing flag (05:18 UTC).
- Performed a controlled traffic ramp and validation before full return-to-service (07:03 UTC).

Customer impact and scope:
- Impacted customers: ~12% of active production traffic in us-west-2 during the incident window; roughly 1,100 active API keys observed at elevated latency or errors.
- SLA: For customers with strict latency SLOs, the incident may have contributed to brief SLO deviations; outreach by CSMs is recommended for affected enterprise customers.

Workarounds and guidance for customers:
- Temporary workaround: If you experienced retries or errors, please retry requests; the platform will respect idempotency where applicable. For time-sensitive workloads, consider using the dedicated routing override (contact Redwood support) to pin requests to Dedicated pools.

Longer-term remediation (high level):
- Add kernel-version compatibility checks to the deployment gating pipeline.
- Expand canary sample sizes and include representative traffic patterns from heavy customers.
- Introduce automated routing sanity checks that validate mapping coverage and fallbacks before a flag is enabled.
- Post-deploy smoke tests to exercise generation at scale for 30 minutes with synthetic traffic mix.

Timeline (UTC) — brief
- 02:17: First elevated latency alerts from synthetic monitors and customer-reported errors (Pager triggered)
- 02:30: On-call SREs confirmed increased error rates; tentative suspect: routing changes deployed 02:10
- 02:45: Initial rollback of routing flag initiated
- 03:10: Engineering confirmed a subset of nodes still draining; started targeted scale-up of stable pool
- 05:18: Faulty routing flag fully disabled; draining of incompatible nodes ongoing
- 07:03: Traffic validation completed; user-visible service restored
- 08:20: Post-incident customer triage and measurement of impacted API keys completed

Open items / questions for engineering (internal)
- Verify root-cause artifacts for deployment tooling (logs + diffs) and attach to internal postmortem.
- Decide rollout timeline for kernel-compat checks and automation (owner: infra-deploy)
- Confirm whether quota/backpressure improvements are required for mixed-version pools.

Suggested customer FAQ (short)
Q: Was customer data exposed? A: No. The incident caused service degradation only; no data exfiltration or modification occurred.
Q: Will I be compensated? A: If you experienced measurable SLO breaches, our customer success team will reach out. For enterprise contracts, compensation eligibility follows contract terms; please contact your CSM.
Q: How will you prevent this from happening again? A: We have concrete actions (listed above) and will share a more detailed timeline for technical fixes in the internal postmortem.

Communications plan / owners
- Publish status.redwood.ai update (owner: customer-success; SLA: within 2 hours of drafting) — drafts below.
- Email to affected enterprise customers (owner: CSM team; draft available in linked artifacts)
- Public blog post? No — incident limited to a region; only customers and status page will be notified.

Draft status page blurb (short version)
"Resolved: A routing configuration change caused elevated latency and intermittent errors for text-generation endpoints in us-west-2 between 02:17 and 07:03 UTC on 2026-11-29. The change has been reverted and services restored. We are performing further hardening to prevent recurrence."

Notes / draft edits (working)
- Confirm exact number of customer API keys impacted (engineering to confirm by 2026-12-01 14:00 UTC).
- Remove any technical leak in customer-facing text (avoid internal flags/implementation details) — keep phrasing to 'routing configuration change'.
- Confirm compensation eligibility list (finance + legal + CSM).

Contacts
- Primary customer contact (CS lead): Aisha Patel — aisha@redwood.ai
- On-call SRE: Miguel Santos — miguel@redwood.ai
- Engineering owner (infra deploy): Omar Haddad — omar@redwood.ai

Appendix: internal links and logs
- Internal deep-dive (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/INC-4512
- Jira incident: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4512
- Infra PR rollback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789
- Slack incident channel: #incident-4512

End of draft — please add comments inline and tag me for approvals before publishing.
